explanation:
I found no single Mathlib declaration that states this result. The theorem says: if the processes C i are independent pre-Brownian motions, then for any finite set S and time t, the vector (C i t) for i in S has law equal to the product of copies of gaussianReal 0 t.

Where I looked:
- Mathlib/Probability/BrownianMotion/Basic.lean defines IsPreBrownianReal. It only has single-process lemmas such as hasLaw_eval, hasLaw_sub, neg, smul and shift. Nothing there covers families of independent Brownian motions or multidimensional Brownian motion.
- The closest general results are iIndepFun.map_fun_eq_pi_map (Probability/Independence/Basic.lean), which the current proof uses, and iIndepFun.hasLaw_pi (Probability/HasLaw.lean). Both need independence of a finite family of random variables. Here the hypothesis is independence of whole path-valued processes indexed by I.

To use either lemma, you first have to turn that hypothesis into independence of the time-t evaluations over S. That takes two more independence lemmas, iIndepFun.precomp and iIndepFun.comp, and then you add the Gaussian law from IsPreBrownianReal.hasLaw_eval. The resulting derivation is short, but it combines several Mathlib results beyond the allowed routine glue. So it is not a special case of one declaration.
